The grid supply includes GML alongside the ASCII file.
The grid GML supplies location, grid spacing and vertical-reference metadata.
The GML also carries spatial-reference information in a software-independent form.
Each ASCII-grid height is calculated for the centre of its pixel.
The ASCII presentation begins from the north-west corner in the map header.
Rows are ordered from west to east.
Each successive row starts 50 metres farther south.
Each grid pixel is 50 metres by 50 metres.
ASCII height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
The .asc file contains the Esri ASCII grid data.
The .gml file enables the grid data to be loaded as GML.
The .prj file contains the spatial-reference system in Esri format.
The .asc.aux.xml file carries default Esri styling parameters.
Each grid tile includes a metadata XML file with information such as flying date.
The ASCII header includes an ncols value.
The ASCII header includes an nrows value.
The ASCII header includes the lower-left easting.
The ASCII header includes the lower-left northing.
The ASCII header records a 50 metre cell size.
Terrain 50 contour layers are supplied as GML 3.2.1.
Using the contour GML requires understanding XML and XML schemas.
Each contour tile includes a GML data file.
Each contour tile includes metadata XML with survey information.
Spot heights are created by an automated selection process.
The process selects the highest mass point within each closed contour.
A spot height equal to its enclosing contour is removed.
A spot height may be lower than its surrounding contour because of a genuine depression.
Contour-supply spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places.
The contour GML model is feature-based.
ContourLine is a distinct feature type.
SpotHeight is a distinct feature type.
LandWaterBoundary is a distinct feature type.
ContourLine propertyValue is represented as a distance.
Contour line types include master, ordinary and auxiliary.
The master subtype corresponds to the traditional index-contour term.
The ordinary subtype corresponds to the traditional standard-contour term.
SpotHeight propertyValue stores the elevation above the applicable British datum.
Current spot-height features use the generic subtype.
LandWaterBoundary supports mean-high, mean-low and Scottish spring-water categories.
